g: alégrense en el Señor
alégrense is an affirmative ustedes command of alegrarse; the reflexive se is attached.
e: Por lo demás
A transition phrase meaning ‘finally’ or ‘as for the rest’; it does not necessarily signal the letter’s end.

g: Cuídense de esos
Cuídense is an affirmative ustedes command of cuidarse de; the preposition de follows the pronoun.
e: esos que mutilan el cuerpo
esos que identifies a group by a relative clause: ‘those who mutilate the body’.

g: la circuncisión somos nosotros
The predicate noun is fronted for emphasis; somos nosotros identifies ‘we’ as the circumcision.
e: por medio del Espíritu de Dios
por medio de is a multiword preposition meaning ‘by means of’ or ‘through’.

g: Si cualquier otro cree tener
After si, present indicative cree presents a real possibility; tener remains an infinitive after cree.
e: yo más
An elliptical comparison: ‘I [have] more’; the repeated verb is understood from the preceding clause.

g: circuncidado al octavo día
circuncidado is a past participle used as a descriptive fragment; al marks the time, ‘on the eighth day’.
e: hebreo de pura cepa
de pura cepa is an idiom for being genuine or thoroughly of a particular stock.

g: en cuanto al celo
en cuanto a means ‘as for’ and introduces another item in Paul’s credential list.
e: la justicia que la ley exige
que is the direct object of exige and refers to justicia: ‘the righteousness the law requires’.

g: todo aquello que para mí era ganancia
que begins a relative clause describing aquello; era is imperfect for the former evaluation.
e: por causa de Cristo
This phrase means ‘because of Christ’ and explains the basis for counting gain as loss.

g: lo he perdido todo
lo he perdido is present perfect with lo referring to the whole set of things; todo reinforces completeness.
e: a fin de ganar a Cristo
a fin de + infinitive is a formal purpose phrase: ‘in order to gain Christ’.

g: No quiero mi propia justicia
No + present quiero directly negates what Paul wants; propia emphasizes ‘my own’.
e: mediante la fe en Cristo
mediante is a formal preposition meaning ‘through’ or ‘by means of’.

g: llegar a ser semejante
llegar a ser means ‘come to be’; semejante is an adjective taking a after it here.
e: participar en sus sufrimientos
participar en means ‘share in’; en introduces the experience being shared.

g: Así espero alcanzar
esperar + infinitive expresses a hoped-for action; así links it with the previous aim.
e: de entre los muertos
de entre means ‘from among’; it distinguishes resurrection from the dead as a group.

g: No es que ya lo haya conseguido
No es que is followed by subjunctive haya conseguido, rejecting an assumed conclusion.
e: sigo adelante
seguir adelante means ‘keep going’ or ‘press on’; it is a movement metaphor.

g: una cosa hago
The object una cosa is placed first for focus; hago is first-person present, ‘I do’.
e: lo que queda atrás
lo que means ‘what’; queda atrás describes what is left behind.

g: sigo avanzando hacia la meta
sigo + gerund expresses continuing action: ‘I keep advancing toward the goal’.
e: el premio que Dios ofrece
que introduces a relative clause; it is the object of ofrece and refers to premio.

g: Todos debemos tener
debemos + infinitive expresses shared obligation; Todos is the plural subject.
e: les hará ver esto
hacer ver means ‘make someone see’; les is the indirect object, ‘make you see this’.

g: vivamos de acuerdo con
vivamos is a first-person plural subjunctive used as an exhortation: ‘let us live in accord with’.
e: En todo caso
A connective meaning ‘in any case’ or ‘at any rate’, narrowing the practical conclusion.

g: sigan todos mi ejemplo
sigan is an affirmative ustedes command; todos emphasizes that the whole group is addressed.
e: conforme al modelo
conforme a means ‘according to’ or ‘in conformity with’.

g: Como les he dicho
Como means ‘as’ here; les he dicho is present perfect, ‘I have told you’.
e: enemigos de la cruz de Cristo
enemigos de identifies hostility toward something; de la cruz specifies what they oppose.

g: se enorgullecen de lo que es su vergüenza
enorgullecerse de takes de; lo que is a neuter clause meaning ‘that which is’.
e: Solo piensan en lo terrenal
lo terrenal turns an adjective into ‘earthly things’; solo limits the scope to these things.

g: somos ciudadanos del cielo
somos is first-person plural; del contracts de + el before cielo.
e: de donde anhelamos recibir
de donde means ‘from where’; the relative adverb connects heaven with the expected Savior.

g: para que sea como su cuerpo
para que + subjunctive sea introduces the result of transformará.
e: mediante el poder con que somete
con que means ‘with which’; it refers back to the power as the means of subjecting all things.
